purpose: Rosuvastatin is used to lower your 'bad' cholesterol (LDL) and triglycerides while raising your 'good' cholesterol (HDL). It helps reduce your risk of heart attack, stroke, and other heart-related problems. Doctors often prescribe it along with a healthy diet and exercise.
how_it_works: Your liver naturally makes cholesterol, and this medicine works by blocking a key enzyme the liver uses to produce it. With less cholesterol being made, your liver pulls more of the 'bad' cholesterol out of your bloodstream to use instead. Over time, this lowers the amount of harmful cholesterol circulating in your blood.
common_side_effects: Muscle aches or weakness are the most talked-about side effects. You might also notice headache, nausea, stomach pain, constipation, or feeling a little tired. Most people tolerate it very well.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have severe muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness — especially with fever or dark-colored urine, as this can rarely signal a serious muscle problem called rhabdomyolysis. This medicine can affect your liver, so avoid heavy alcohol use and let your doctor know if you have liver problems. Do NOT take this medication if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm a developing baby.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 to 10 mg once daily, taken with or without food. Your doctor may increase it up to 40 mg per day depending on your cholesterol levels and how you respond. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
